column1: # Shared fixture for gitbackup's three live-log "is this operation over yet"
# regexes (ticket 29, D11). Unlike cron.tsv (ticket 06/12), there is no
# shell-side implementation of "is this line terminal" to compare against --
# only the three JS regexes below decide that. What drifts instead is the
# TEXT: shell prints a message, JS matches a literal fragment of it, and the
# two sides used to know that fragment independently (ticket 19 renamed a
# restore.sh message and the JS regex kept the old text -- the poller never
# noticed the operation had finished at all).
# So this file is read two different ways, proving two different things:
#     schedule-adjacent section) greps the <anchor> column against the
#     proof that every <line> here is not invented, it is what gb_log/
#     gb_die/printf in the shell actually emit. A subset of rows (see that
#     test's own comment for which) is additionally driven through the REAL
#     CLI/functions against a real local bare git repository and the actual
#     captured output is checked against <line> -- stronger than a grep,
#     because it proves the message survives quoting/interpolation intact,
#     not just that the literal fragment appears somewhere in the source
#     from settings.js, GB_RESTORE_TERMINAL_RE from history.js) and checks
#     each <line> against the regexvar it names, asserting .test(line)
# Neither test alone catches every drift. Together: a shell rename not
# reflected here fails the grep (or the real-code-path) half; a rename
# reflected here but not mirrored in the regex fails the JS half. See the
# ticket 29 report for exactly what each half does and does not prove.
# Format: tab-separated, four columns, one case per line.

column3: <line>

column1: # GB_RESTORE_TERMINAL_RE -- the exact variable name, because GB_LOG_TERMINAL_RE
# is shared by Overview's own handleRun AND handleTest (see overview.js's own
# comment above that regex); it is not "one row per shell subcommand".
# <terminal> is "yes" or "no". <line> is a plausible real log line (dynamic
# values like commit ids/branches/urls are realistic placeholders, not the
# literal shell source). <anchor> is a short fixed substring of <line> that
# appears byte-for-byte in the shell source that emits it -- i.e. <line>
# minus the interpolated ($_gb_*) parts. None of the four fields ever
# overview.js: Overview's own "Backup now" AND "Test connection" buttons
# both poll against this one regex.
# -- terminal: yes (one row per alternative in the regex) --
